grid: Ending 25 · A city with its lights on
You isolate the circuit feeding the spare room. Along every street, the lamps brighten. Mother calls from a house with one fewer door.
dawn: You sit beside the porter and wait until daylight. When the next bus arrives, the passengers are ordinary strangers. For once, nobody knows your name.
witness: You watch the film, then tell the archivist exactly what you saw. This time, there is a witness outside the house. Mother can no longer be made to forget.
keeper: You choose to remain, with a warning on the fuse box and the lantern beside the door. The house does not stop whispering. You learn when not to listen.

noteDefs.title: BEFORE YOU LEAVE
noteDefs.text:
The gate knows three words.
First: WE.
Do not knock back.

noteDefs.title: DON’T FEED IT
noteDefs.text:
Second: WERE.
The sandwiches appear because
someone keeps setting your place.

noteDefs.title: COUNT THE CHAIRS
noteDefs.text:
Third: HERE.
Say all three at the garden gate.
Take nobody’s reflection with you.

noteDefs.title: THE GARDENER
noteDefs.text:
Turn the music box in the shed.
Take its lullaby to the well.
Do not look down while it sings.

noteDefs.title: PLEASE REMEMBER
noteDefs.text:
If every note is found,
write your own name in the diary.
You are allowed to be whole.

noteDefs.title: UNDER THE MIRROR
noteDefs.text:
The glass remembers the room.
Sometimes it remembers someone
who is no longer standing there.

truth:
Mother steps into the room beside you. She tells the child everything she made herself forget.
The walls loosen like a held breath. Two voices become one.
At breakfast, there are three places at the table.
escape:
The telephone rings once. You take Mother’s hand and open the front door.
Beyond it is a street you recognise. At every window stands your reflection.
You keep walking.
ward:
The mirror steps across the chalk circle. It takes the diary and all the memories it contains.
“Someone must keep them,” it says.
You and Mother leave. At night, every mirror in your new home faces the wall.
gate:
You speak the three words. The gate opens onto a morning that has not happened yet.
The house calls after you in Mother’s voice. This time, you do not answer.
well:
The music box sings into the well. A child finishes the song from somewhere far beneath the water.
When you return to the house, the spare room is a cupboard.
Every night, a new flower grows beside the well.
whole:
You write your own name over both names in the diary.
The mirror cracks without breaking. Mother remembers a single child, with every memory intact.
The sticky notes disappear. You leave one of your own: “We got out.”
morning: Ending X · A garden for tomorrow

At dawn, every flower faces the house. You invite Mother outside.
She names the flowers instead of naming the things she lost.
For the first time, the diary has no entry for tomorrow.
burial: Ending XI · What the earth keeps

You leave the memory beneath the roots. The spare room fills with the smell of rain.
Mother remembers love without remembering the room.
Every autumn, you find one small brass leaf beneath the tree.
light:
The lantern lights a path beyond the garden. You follow the shadow that moves exactly when you do.
Behind you, the house keeps calling your name.
You let the flame answer.

burn:
The photograph and recording prove that you were here. You burn the diary. The door becomes a patch of wallpaper.
Mother finally says your name.
That night, you hear a child crying inside the wall.
enter:
You enter the room. The figure has your face at seven years old.
“I kept everything you couldn’t bear,” it says.
You sit beside it. Downstairs, Mother calls both your names.
For the first time, you answer together.
release:
You unlock the door. Someone wearing your face walks downstairs.
Mother embraces them. “You’re finally home.”
You try to follow, but the hallway ends at a bedroom. On its desk is a diary.
You pick up the pen.
